title: Behavioral Economics Framing Effects on Preference Labels

original_idea.body:
# Behavioral Economics Framing Effects on Preference Labels

**Problem:** Preference labels may be swayed by gain/loss framing, biasing reward models toward presentation.

**Direction:** Present a judge with gain- vs loss-framed equivalent pairs, measure reversals; test whether an RM trained on such data inherits the bias.

**Why it matters:** Models may learn to optimize framing. No lab resources.

**Relevant context:** CBEval arXiv:2412.03605; KTO; arXiv:2503.11701.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Framing bias corrupting reward signals is real but the chain to catastrophic risk is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference framing experiments plus an optional small RM train; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused preference-reversal measurement; the RM-inheritance step adds a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open judges, no lab data; independent-friendly fuzzy-reward auditing.

low_compute.reasoning: Mostly inference plus optionally a small RM train; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: LLM framing sensitivity is well documented.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: LLM framing sensitivity is extensively documented.
